publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Satellite Distress and Safety Systems
abstract: COSPAS-SARSAT is an international satellite system for search and rescue. It consists of a constellation of satellites in polar orbit and a network of earth stations which provide distress alert and location information to appropriate rescue authorities, anywhere in the world, for maritime, aviation and land users in distress. The author describes the system, looking at: the space segment; ground segment; beacons; 121.5 MHz local coverage; 406 MHz global coverage; and alert data distribution. The global system performance is reported following system waiting time and location acquisition probability experiments. Future developments and use for GMDSS, aviation and personal locator beacons are briefly discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Potential for a greater satellite technology role in aeronautical safety communications
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Satellite Distress and Safety Systems
abstract: The author discusses the benefits to aviation of reliable communication. Use of satellite CNS (communication, navigation and surveillance) allows for automatic position reporting. When GPS/Glonass satellite navigation joins satcom, derived positions will be accurate to 100 m. Other benefits such as automatic air traffic control functions are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Possibilities of using satellites for lone worker alarms
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Satellite Distress and Safety Systems
abstract: The safety of individuals when working by themselves is a continuing problem for many organisations. The National Rivers Authority (NRA) have a significant number of employees who, in the course of their duties, will be alone in the countryside of England and Wales. Kennedy and Donkin Systems Control Limited (KDSC) has been commissioned by the NRA to investigate the feasibility of providing a means by which employees working alone could summon assistance. The authors give a brief overview of the concept of a lone worker alarm (LWA) and the possible use of satellites in providing the LWA facilities.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Integration of maritime distress and safety satellite communications with commercial services
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Satellite Distress and Safety Systems
abstract: The author explains how commercial communication improves safety because ship owners are inclined to use good equipment to increase efficiency. In an emergency, operators will be familiar with the equipment, and since it is used routinely, any faults will be noticed quickly. It is necessary to have a call priority system and responsible use of the system. Having discussed that, the author looks at safety system costs.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Satellite Distress and Safety Systems
abstract: The role of INMARSAT in the Global Maritime Distress and Safety System (GMDSS) is divided into two areas: space segment provision for instant reliable distress and safety communication; and two basic satellite communication systems for GMDSS medium and long range communication. To discuss these roles, the author looks at the INMARSAT land earth stations, space segment and mobile earth stations (or ship earth stations). Finally the performance of several GMDSS functions using INMARSAT is explained.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Capabilities of satellite technology for land mobile safety communications
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Satellite Distress and Safety Systems
abstract: Land mobile safety communications are already catered for in many communications systems. The author illustrates the capabilities of satellite technology by defining the general requirements of safety communications, with reference to existing practises, and examining how those requirements are being met. The mechanism used is to answer a number of questions which might be asked by a potential user of land mobile safety communications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Dissemination of maritime safety information by satellite
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Satellite Distress and Safety Systems
abstract: The broadcast of maritime safety information (MSI) is a core function of modern maritime communications. The author explains what MSI is and the three main sources from which it comes: IMO/IHO World-Wide Navigational Warnings Service; national meteorological organisations; and national search and rescue authorities. The broadcast of MSI using the INMARSAT SafetyNET service and FleetNET service is discussed. In particular the SafetyNET coded preamble, C-codes, are explained.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
